answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring every new identity to post a time-locked bond that only unlocks after three consecutive epochs of peer-attested original work. The bond sits on a public ledge of locked capital; each extra fake multiplies the total stake an attacker must freeze. Like a fable of ants building one shared mound, the cost scales with headcount and cannot be parallelized across an ocean of cheap clones, because each clone still needs its own attested work history before the bond releases.
